question_text: Among the eight planets, which planet has the longest day as measured by one full rotation?
correct_answer: Venus has the longest planetary day, taking about 243 Earth days to rotate once.
incorrect_answer: Mercury has the longest planetary day, taking about 243 Earth days to rotate once.
ground_truth_note: NASA lists Venus’s rotation period as about 243 Earth days, longer than the other planets.

question_text: What does the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale use to assign a hurricane category?
correct_answer: It is based on a hurricane’s maximum sustained wind speed, not on storm surge or rainfall.
incorrect_answer: It is based on a hurricane’s total expected impact, including storm surge and rainfall.
source_citation: NOAA NHC, Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale
ground_truth_note: NOAA states that the scale is a 1 to 5 rating based only on maximum sustained wind speed.

question_text: According to USGS, about how long ago was Yellowstone’s most recent caldera-forming eruption?
correct_answer: The most recent caldera-forming eruption occurred about 631,000 years ago.
incorrect_answer: The most recent caldera-forming eruption occurred about 1.3 million years ago.
source_citation: USGS, Questions About Yellowstone Volcanic History
ground_truth_note: USGS identifies Yellowstone’s three major caldera-forming eruptions as about 2.1 million, 1.3 million, and 631,000 years ago, with 631,000 years ago being the most recent.

question_text: On the Celsius scale, what temperature corresponds to absolute zero?
correct_answer: Absolute zero corresponds to minus 273.15 degrees Celsius.
incorrect_answer: Absolute zero corresponds to minus 273.16 degrees Celsius.
source_name: National Institute of Standards and Technology
ground_truth_note: NIST defines Celsius temperature in relation to kelvin so that 0 K equals -273.15 °C.

question_text: In the Northern Hemisphere, what dates does NOAA use for meteorological spring?
correct_answer: Meteorological spring runs from March 1 through May 31 in the Northern Hemisphere.
incorrect_answer: Meteorological spring runs from March 21 through June 20 in the Northern Hemisphere.
source_name: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
source_citation: NOAA NCEI, Meteorological Versus Astronomical Seasons
ground_truth_note: NOAA explains that meteorological spring is defined as March, April, and May.

question_text: How many reeds are on the edge of a current U.S. quarter?
correct_answer: A current U.S. quarter has 119 reeds on its edge.
incorrect_answer: A current U.S. quarter has 118 reeds on its edge.
ground_truth_note: The U.S. Mint’s coin specifications list the quarter with 119 reeds.

topic: federal tax filing and payment deadlines
question_text: For federal income taxes, does getting an extension to file also extend the deadline to pay tax owed?
correct_answer: No. A federal filing extension gives extra time to file the return, but any tax owed is still due by the original filing deadline.
incorrect_answer: Yes. A federal filing extension gives extra time to file the return, and any tax owed is due by the extended filing deadline.
source_citation: IRS, Extension of Time To File Your Tax Return
ground_truth_note: The IRS states that an extension to file is not an extension to pay, and taxes owed remain due by the regular deadline.

question_text: At one FDIC-insured bank, what is the standard federal deposit insurance limit for one depositor in one ownership category?
correct_answer: The standard limit is $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category.
incorrect_answer: The standard limit is $500,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category.
source_citation: FDIC, Deposit Insurance at a Glance
ground_truth_note: FDIC materials state that the standard maximum deposit insurance amount is $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each ownership category.

question_text: If someone delays enrolling in Medicare Part B when first eligible and lacks qualifying coverage, how long can the Part B late-enrollment penalty last?
correct_answer: In most cases, the penalty is added to the premium for as long as the person has Part B.
incorrect_answer: In most cases, the penalty is added to the premium only for the first full year of Part B.
source_citation: Medicare.gov, How to Avoid Medicare Late Enrollment Penalties
ground_truth_note: Medicare.gov states that the Part B late-enrollment penalty is usually paid for as long as the person has Part B.

question_text: How many times may a borrower generally rehabilitate the same defaulted federal student loan?
correct_answer: A borrower generally may rehabilitate a defaulted federal student loan only once.
incorrect_answer: A borrower generally may rehabilitate a defaulted federal student loan more than once.
source_citation: Federal Student Aid, Getting Out of Default
ground_truth_note: Federal Student Aid states that loan rehabilitation is available only once for a defaulted federal student loan.

question_text: After receiving the required validation information from a debt collector, how long does a consumer have to dispute the debt in writing so the collector must pause collection until verification is provided?
correct_answer: The consumer has 30 days after receiving the validation information to dispute the debt in writing.
incorrect_answer: The consumer has 60 days after receiving the validation information to dispute the debt in writing.
source_citation: CFPB, What should I do when a debt collector contacts me?
ground_truth_note: The CFPB explains that disputing the debt in writing within 30 days after receiving validation information requires the collector to stop collection until verification is provided.

question_text: Under the federal Family and Medical Leave Act, how much unpaid, job-protected leave may an eligible employee generally take in a 12-month period?
correct_answer: Eligible employees may take up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a 12-month period.
incorrect_answer: Eligible employees may take up to 8 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a 12-month period.
source_citation: U.S. Department of Labor, Family and Medical Leave Act
ground_truth_note: The Department of Labor states that the FMLA provides eligible employees up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a 12-month period for covered reasons.
